page: Amazon Web Services c6g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton processors utilizing the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at 2.5 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. Cache resources include 64 KB L1D cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48574.31 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11649.0. Single-core performance is comparatively weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 20.33 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block cached speed of 1894.03 GB/sec, which drops to 163.55 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. The instance demonstrates average throughput for static web serving at 33.12 GB/sec and software compilation at 25603.0.

The ARM-based architecture provides qualitative cost efficiency by delivering a high density of dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, which reduces resource contention compared to traditional x86 architectures. This makes the c6g.8xlarge appropriate for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and medium-scale language model inference.
